items.name: Medu vada
items.prabhava: The classical vataka — urad dal ground and deep-fried; nourishing but among the heaviest of breakfast foods.
combinations: dunked in hot sambar (softens and lightens)
with coconut chutney
black pepper and curry leaf in the batter aid digestion
contraindications: skin conditions aggravated by urad + frying
items.preparation: Soaked urad dal ground fluffy, shaped into rings and deep-fried. Eat hot and fresh with sambar; a cold vada is a brick. One or two, not a plateful.

items.name: Besan pakora
combinations: monsoon pairing with hot masala chai
mint chutney (the pungent cuts the grease)
ajwain in the batter — traditional digestive insurance
items.preparation: Vegetables dipped in spiced besan batter and deep-fried. A monsoon indulgence, not a habit — fresh oil, hot serving, ajwain in the batter, small portion.

items.name: Sooji halwa (sheera)
items.prabhava: Prasad of the North — ghee-roasted semolina is the traditional gentle strengthener for convalescents and new mothers.
combinations: cardamom, saffron and a few raisins
with puri and chana (halwa-puri, festival trio)
warm milk for a deeper brimhana effect
items.preparation: Semolina roasted patiently in ghee until aromatic, then cooked with hot water or milk and sugar. The roasting is everything — raw-tasting sheera sits heavy.
provenance: North Indian temple and postpartum tradition

items.name: Moong dal halwa
items.prabhava: Rajasthan's winter strengthener — mung's lightness is deliberately traded away through ghee and slow roasting to build deep warmth and bulk.
combinations: cardamom, saffron, slivered almonds
small portion after a light meal
wedding-season indulgence with warm milk
items.preparation: Soaked ground mung roasted in generous ghee for the better part of an hour, then sweetened. Reserve for deep winter and strong digestion; a little goes far.

items.name: Besan ladoo
combinations: cardamom and chopped nuts within
with warm milk as a winter breakfast (traditional)
after exercise — the wrestler's sweet
items.preparation: Besan roasted low and slow in ghee until nutty, bound with powdered sugar into rounds. Well-roasted flour digests far better than hastily made ladoos.

items.name: Til-gud ladoo
items.prabhava: The Sankranti sweet — sesame and jaggery, both ushna and snigdha, made into winter's answer to vata: warming, lubricating, strengthening.
combinations: exchanged at Makar Sankranti (til-gul ghya)
with warm milk in deep winter
dry ginger powder added in some regional versions
items.preparation: Roasted sesame bound in melted jaggery and rolled warm. Classical winter logic: tila for the joints and skin, guda for warmth and blood.

items.name: Peanut chikki
combinations: winter travel snack
with warm milk
sesame-peanut mixed chikkis (Sankranti)
items.preparation: Roasted peanuts set in hard jaggery brittle. Dense winter energy in a slab — one piece is a snack, the whole bar is a meal.

items.name: Steamed modak
items.prabhava: Ganapati's offering — rice-flour shell steamed around coconut-jaggery; being steamed rather than fried, it is the gentlest of festival sweets.
combinations: ghee spooned over at serving (traditional)
cardamom and nutmeg in the filling
festival meal centerpiece at Ganesh Chaturthi
items.preparation: Soft rice-flour dough pleated around a coconut-jaggery-cardamom filling and steamed. Eat warm with ghee; the fried version is a different, heavier dravya.

items.name: Puran poli
combinations: ghee poured generously on top (non-negotiable, traditionally)
with warm milk or katachi amti (the spiced dal-water counterpoint)
festival midday meal
items.preparation: Chana dal cooked with jaggery into puran, stuffed in thin wheat dough and roasted. The traditional ghee and the sour-spiced amti alongside exist to make it digestible.

items.name: Shrikhand
items.prabhava: The classical shikharini — hung curd whipped with sugar, saffron and cardamom; celebrated in medieval texts as delicious, nourishing and decidedly heavy.
combinations: with hot puri (Gujarati festival pairing — the heat balances the cold)
saffron, cardamom, charoli nuts
mango pulp version (amrakhand) in season
viruddha: with fish at the same meal
items.preparation: Curd hung until thick, whisked with sugar and aromatics. A summer-midday festival dish; classical texts pair rich curd sweets with hot fried breads to offset the cold heaviness.

items.name: Basundi
combinations: with hot puri (the classic pairing)
cardamom, saffron, nutmeg
sharad purnima moonlight tradition (kheer family)
viruddha: with sour fruits at the same meal
items.preparation: Milk simmered and stirred down to half or less, sweetened and spiced. Deeply brimhana; a festival portion is small, taken at midday when agni can meet it.
provenance: kshirapaka logic per classical dairy texts

items.name: Rabri
combinations: over jalebi or malpua (festival stacking — very heavy)
cardamom and pistachios
small clay-pot servings (the traditional portion control)
items.preparation: Milk reduced slowly on a wide pan, the cream layers gathered as lachha. Richest of the milk sweets — a few spoonfuls at midday, not a bowl at night.

items.name: Coconut chutney
combinations: with idli, dosa, vada (the standard trio)
green chili and ginger ground in
mustard-urad tempering on top
contraindications: same-day-only freshness — stale coconut chutney turns fast
items.preparation: Fresh coconut ground with green chili, ginger and roasted chana dal, tempered with mustard and curry leaves. Eat fresh; refrigerated leftovers lose both taste and virtue.

items.name: Mint chutney
items.prabhava: Rare combination — pungent yet cooling; sharpens digestion without stoking pitta, which is why it rides alongside every fried snack.
combinations: with pakoras and samosas (cuts the grease)
coriander leaves blended in (the standard hari chutney)
a spoon of curd for chaat versions
contraindications: reflux in sensitive individuals (mint relaxes the sphincter)
items.preparation: Fresh mint and coriander ground with green chili, lemon and salt. Made fresh daily — the volatile oils that do the digestive work fade within hours.

items.name: Mango pickle (achar)
items.prabhava: A condiment-dose agni trigger — one sliver wakes salivation and appetite at the start of a meal; classical sandhita (preserved) foods are potent in small amounts only.
combinations: with curd rice (the classic counterpoint)
with theplas and parathas (travel pairing)
a sliver with khichdi for flavour lift
items.preparation: Raw mango cured with salt, red chili, fenugreek, mustard and oil, matured in the sun. Strictly a condiment — a teaspoon beside the plate, not a side dish.

items.name: Urad papad
items.prabhava: Classical parpata — the roasted wafer taken to spark digestion and cut through a rich meal; alkaline papad-khar gives it its bite.
combinations: roasted (not fried) beside dal-rice
crushed over khichdi
with curd rice
contraindications: fried papads for kapha and weight management
items.preparation: Urad dough with papad-khar rolled paper-thin, sun-dried, then flame-roasted or fried. Roasted is the digestive version; fried is a different, heavier proposition.

items.name: Nutgrass tuber
items.prabhava: Deepana-pachana-grahi in one root — kindles agni, digests ama and binds loose stool; the classical first answer to summer diarrhea and fever-digestion.
combinations: with ginger for ama with cold signs
musta-parpataka decoction for fevers (classical)
in shadanga paniya (six-herb fever water)
items.preparation: Dried tuber as decoction or fine powder, 1–3 g. One of the rare bitters that is cooling yet digestive — suits pitta-season gut trouble precisely.

items.name: Dried hibiscus
items.prabhava: Classical japa is the hair-and-pitta flower — cooling to the blood and scalp; as a tart infusion it cools the system in the manner of sour-cold summer drinks.
combinations: cold infusion with rock sugar in summer
with rose petals for a deeper pitta cooler
hair-oil infusions (external classical use)
items.preparation: Dried calyces steeped hot or cold into a tart crimson infusion; sweeten lightly. Internal use is gentle; the classical literature leans on japa for hair and pitta-rakta.

items.name: Rose petal preserve
items.prabhava: The classical pitta-shamaka preserve — sun-cured rose and sugar that cools burning eyes, acid stomachs and hot tempers alike; a gentle laxative for pitta types.
combinations: a spoon in warm milk at bedtime (pitta insomnia)
in paan (traditional digestive finish)
with praval or mukta pishti in formal pitta protocols
items.preparation: Fresh damask rose petals layered with sugar and slow-cured in sunlight for weeks. One to two teaspoons; summer mornings are its natural hour.

items.name: Bael leaf
items.prabhava: Shiva's trifoliate offering — folk-classical use of the fresh leaf juice for blood-sugar and ama; distinct from the fruit, which works on the gut.
combinations: fresh leaf juice with black pepper (folk diabetic morning dose)
in dashamula-family decoctions (bilva is a dashamula root, leaves used adjunctively)
items.reviewNote: Leaf virya given as ushna per predraft hint and dashamula-bilva convention; some nighantu passages treat bilva parts differently — expert should confirm leaf-specific virya.
items.preparation: Two to three fresh leaves chewed or juiced in the morning, or dried-leaf infusion. Traditional metabolic adjunct; the fruit, not the leaf, is the diarrhea remedy.

items.name: Jamun seed powder
items.prabhava: The traditional madhumeha (diabetes) powder — jambu seed's astringency is credited with steadying sugar and binding loose stool.
combinations: with lukewarm water before food (folk dosing)
with methi and karela in metabolic blends
buttermilk vehicle for loose motions
items.preparation: Sun-dried jamun kernels powdered fine; half to one teaspoon with water before meals. Astringent and drying — buffer with buttermilk if the gut runs dry.

items.name: Shilajit
items.prabhava: Yogavahi — the great carrier: taken with other rasayanas it drives them deeper into the tissues; classical texts call purified shilajatu a rasayana for strength, metabolism and madhumeha.
combinations: with warm milk (classical vehicle for strength)
with triphala for metabolic use
rice-grain to pea-sized dose dissolved in warm water
viruddha: classical caution: avoid with horse gram (kulattha) during shilajit courses
items.preparation: Only purified (shodhita) resin. A rice-grain to pea-sized amount dissolved in warm milk or water, mornings, in courses. Sourcing quality is everything with this dravya.

items.name: Amla juice
items.prabhava: Fresh-pressed amalaki — five rasas, sour-dominant yet cooling, the rare fruit that pacifies all three doshas; the daily rasayana in its most direct form.
combinations: on an empty stomach with honey (classical pairing)
with aloe juice in modern practice
a pinch of turmeric for metabolic support
contraindications: very cold constitutions on cold mornings (take with honey)
items.preparation: Fresh amla pressed and taken 15–30 ml on an empty stomach, ideally with honey. Fresh svarasa outranks bottled; bottled outranks none.

items.name: Sprouted fenugreek
items.prabhava: Sprouting softens methi's harsh bitterness while keeping its metabolic edge — the gentler everyday form of the classical blood-sugar and lactation seed.
combinations: a spoonful on morning salads or poha
with lemon (cuts bitterness further)
postpartum diet alongside methi ladoos
items.preparation: Methi seeds soaked overnight and sprouted 1–2 days; eaten raw by the spoon or lightly steamed. Small daily amounts beat occasional large ones.

items.name: Fresh turmeric root
items.prabhava: Haridra's fresh form — vishaghna (anti-toxic) and raktashodhaka (blood-cleansing); juicier and gentler than the dried powder, favoured in winter pickles and morning shots.
combinations: grated with lemon and salt as winter pickle (fresh haldi achar)
with black pepper (classical bioavailability pairing)
in warm milk with ghee for throat and skin
items.preparation: Fresh rhizome grated into food, pickled, or juiced in small morning doses. Winter is its season — the fresh root arrives at exactly the time kapha begins to build.
